02

Service Catalogue — One Workspace, Any Operation

You define the workspace. A workspace represents the operational domain you want to manage — a city, plant, fleet, programme or theatre. Define its entities, connect the data sources you already operate, and apply the same six services across your domain.

01 · Connect — One Event Contract for Every Source

HTTP ingest plus browser, React, Node, Python, Java, Go, Swift and Android SDKs. Per-event validation, with 1,000 events per request and a 1 MB body limit.

02 · Model — An Ontology in Your Own Terms

Define entities, fields and relations for the domain you operate. Entities are populated from event group keys or explicitly marked as needing a connector. Every definition is versioned and audited.

03 · Govern — Governed Metrics, One Number

Promote an analysis into a named, owned and versioned metric. Dashboards, alerts and answers all resolve through that single definition.

04 · Watch — Detectors, Cases and Alerts

Champion and challenger models assess your entities at a fixed cadence and raise cases. Threshold alerts are evaluated every minute, with state and history.

05 · Analyse — Journeys, Segments and Root Causes

Funnels, paths, retention, cohorts, segments, acquisition and deep analysis — including readings that are only unusual together.

06 · Ask — Ask in English, See the Query

A question becomes a visible, auditable query over your entities. Only schema information and the question reach the model — never raw events.

03

Fundamental Introduction

From Fragmented Telemetry to Self-Governed Operational Decisions

Operations do not lack data. They lack a single, trusted path that transforms a sensor reading into a reliable metric that decision-makers can act upon.

  • One event contract — every asset, reading, alarm and work order arrives through the same ingestion path.
  • One entity model — assets, sites, users and accounts are first-class nouns, versioned and auditable.
  • One governed number — metrics are named, owned and versioned, ensuring deterministic results so that two people asking the same question receive the same answer.
  • One AI path — the model sees schemas and questions, never raw operational data.
04

Why Now: The Industrial Data-to-AI Gap

The Gap Is Trust and Continuity, Not Connectivity

Fragmented

SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) systems, historians, ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) platforms and spreadsheets each hold only part of the picture. Modern systems struggle to reconcile these fragmented sources of information.

Disconnected

Edge bridges may buffer readings for hours, but even delayed batches must be attributed to the correct timestamp and time window.

Ungoverned

Two dashboards, two definitions, two numbers. Decisions stall on whose number is right.

AI-shy

Teams expect actionable insights but are reluctant to send raw operational data to external AI model providers.

05

Ask: A Conversation With Your Own Data

Ask, Then Keep Asking

Plain English in, a sentence and a chart out. A follow-up inherits the thread, so “and orders per day?” needs no restatement.

Plan Before It Runs

Multi-part questions become a checked plan. When the rules do not recognise the shape, the model drafts one from Tangent's tools; nothing runs until you continue.

Sourced, Audited, Honest

Every step cites the rules, the live table or the model. Only event names and schemas reach the model — never raw events.

07

Real-Time Ingestion and Edge Reliability

Built for the Hard Network, Not the Lab Network

  • Per-event validation — one malformed event never loses the other 999, and the response names each refusal by index.
  • At-least-once + de-duplication — retrying is always safe when every event carries a stable ID.
  • Quarantine, not silence — an event that cannot be stored is quarantined with its state, stage and reason.
  • Bounded queues and backoff — SDKs batch events, retry using exponential backoff with jitter, and discard events only when the configured retry budget is exhausted.
  • Restart recovery differs by SDK — browser and Swift persist queued events, whereas server-side SDKs hold queues in memory. Design the ingestion bridge accordingly.

Operational limits are explicit: 1,000 events per request, a 1 MB body limit and a per-key ingestion budget.

08

Entity Graph and Ontology Modelling

Your Nouns, Defined Once

TangentLens models your operations using your own business terminology — such as Asset, Site, Account, User, Release and Work Order. Every analysis and AI-generated answer is restricted to the entities and relationships defined within your workspace.

  • Entities are populated from events or clearly marked as needing a connector.
  • Labels, descriptions and fields are versioned, and every save is audited.
  • Your defined relationships transform a flat event stream into a graph that you can filter and traverse.
  • Assets can be identified from a single group key on an event, without an additional connector.
09

Governed Metrics and the Trust Layer

One Definition, One Owner, One Number

  • Promote to metric — an analysis becomes a named, owned and versioned metric definition.
  • Ownership is mandatory — a metric without an owner cannot be published.
  • Changes are versions — the previous definition is retained, and consumers pinned to it are notified.
  • One path — dashboards, alerts and Ask-in-English all resolve through the governed definition.

Domain Example: Mining — Heavy Equipment, Site Safety and Extraction Tracking

Mining

Operational problem

Fleet health and safety depend on readings from remote sites that report intermittently and inconsistently.

Ingestion

Generate one aggregated sensor_reading per asset per interval. Record alarms and trips as individual events, and represent maintenance interventions as work orders.

Entity model

Assets are the group key, sites are properties, and manufacturer, model and criticality are lifted onto the asset profile.

Governed metrics

Alarm rate per asset, vibration excursions, time-to-work-order, quiet-asset count.

AI insight

Automated anomaly detection compares current readings against each asset's own history. Work orders are evaluated at predefined checkpoints.

ROI outcome

Fewer unplanned stops, faster intervention, auditable safety trails.

11

Domain Example: Manufacturing — IIoT Streams, Defects and Cycle Time

Manufacturing & Assembly Line

Operational problem

Line performance is buried across PLCs, historians and quality systems that never share a timeline.

Ingestion

Interval-based readings per station, defect events with reason codes, maintenance as work orders.

Entity model

Lines and stations are entities, parts and batches are properties, and operators are users.

Governed metrics

OEE components, defect rate, cycle-time variance, maintenance effectiveness.

AI insight

Ask questions in natural language against machine and quality schemas, and analyse segments to identify the factors driving changes in key metrics.

ROI outcome

Higher OEE, lower scrap, shorter changeover.

Domain Example: Social Causes & Non-Profit Impact Tracking

Social Impact & Non-Profit

Operational problem

Funders demand measurable evidence of outcomes, but beneficiary data is often sensitive and fragmented across programmes.

Ingestion

Programme events, beneficiary identity with consent, resource allocation and outcome attestations.

Entity model

Beneficiary, programme, cohort, funder — with privacy and consent fields first-class.

Governed metrics

Reach, completion, cost-per-outcome, retention of beneficiaries.

AI insight

Only schema information leaves the workspace, ensuring that sensitive beneficiary data remains within your environment.

ROI outcome

Defensible impact reporting and better resource allocation.

Domain Example: Retail & Supply Chain

Retail & Supply Chain

Operational problem

Omnichannel customer journeys, inventory and fulfilment processes span multiple systems that lack a unified customer identity.

Ingestion

Ingest orders, shopping carts, product views, revenue records, group memberships and device context.

Entity model

Shopper, account, product and order as entities, with customer entity resolution across sessions.

Governed metrics

Conversion, basket, repeat purchase, campaign return, inventory turns.

AI insight

Root-cause scan across channel, campaign and product segments.

ROI outcome

Conversion lift, lower stockouts, attributable campaign spend.

Domain Example: Oil & Gas — Pipeline Telemetry, Integrity and Compliance

Oil & Gas

Operational problem

Upstream and downstream assets communicate over harsh, low-bandwidth networks, making reliable asset-integrity monitoring and auditable safety evidence essential.

Ingestion

Pressure, temperature, flow and vibration readings, with alarms recorded as events and work orders as interventions.

Entity model

Wells, pipeline segments, facilities and assets as entities, with contracts as group memberships.

Governed metrics

Integrity index, alarm-to-intervention time, throughput, compliance evidence completeness.

AI insight

Apply change-point detection and multivariate analysis to defined features, with explanations identifying the factors driving observed changes.

ROI outcome

Reduced leak risk, faster response, audit-ready compliance.

Domain Example: Military & Defence — Secure Edge, Tactical Tracking

Military & Defence

Operational problem

Mission data arrives from geographically dispersed assets over intermittent, low-bandwidth connections. This data must remain trustworthy even under degraded network conditions.

Ingestion

Compact readings and alarms from field bridges, stable IDs, chunked batches and backoff based on the remaining retry budget.

Entity model

Tactical assets, units and missions as entities, with readiness state as a property.

Governed metrics

Asset readiness, mission tempo, logistics latency, anomaly count.

AI insight

The bring-your-own-endpoint deployment tier keeps all processing within the accredited network.

ROI outcome

Faster decisions under degraded communications and demonstrable data sovereignty.
